dialogue.content: I'm taking a customer's team out to dinner in Denver in October 2026. What's the limit per person?

**$110 per person** for a customer dinner in October 2026.

That's from the **2026 Travel and Expense Policy**, section 8 (Customer entertainment): meals and events with customers or prospects are reimbursable up to $110 per person, counting every attendee including Cardinal employees. (The 2025 policy's $90 limit has been superseded.)

A few conditions that apply:
- Get your manager's approval **before** the event.
- The expense report must list **every attendee** and the business purpose.
- Many of our customers are public utilities with their own gift rules — check the Gifts and entertainment section of the Employee Handbook.

Note this is separate from the $75/day domestic meal limit for your own travel; the customer entertainment limit applies when customers are present.
Great, thanks! One more thing — I've got an $820 flight for that same trip. Does that need any approval beyond my manager's?

**Yes — you'll need your department VP's approval too.**

Per the **Finance Memo: Expense Approval Thresholds**, effective **2026-09-01**, any single expense over **$750** requires approval from your department's vice president, in addition to your manager. This replaces the $1,000 threshold in Section 14 of the 2026.1 Travel and Expense Policy. Your $820 flight is over $750, so it triggers the VP approval.

Two other things worth checking for this trip:
- **Pre-trip approval:** from 2026-09-01, any trip with an estimated total cost over **$2,500** needs your manager's approval in TripDesk before you book (TripDesk will prompt for it automatically).
- **Booking lead time:** book air travel at least **14 days** before departure, and fly economy (premium economy only if the scheduled flight is over 6 hours).

Since your dinner and flight are on the same trip, it's worth confirming the total estimate in TripDesk so you know whether the pre-trip approval rule also applies.
